110	| US-04-BR-16 | "Do not copy brands, logos, names or texts of any real insurer." | No logo, brand name, slogan, illustration or text of any real company appears in the code, assets or screenshots; the reference screenshots are not stored. 111	
112	## 5. Acceptance criteria
113	
114	The story has no Gherkin scenarios, so every AC is derived. Conventions:
115	
116	- "I completed step 1 in Colombia / Chile" uses the values of US-01-AC-04 / US-02 §5 conventions;
117	  the date is typed as "15/05/1990" (stored "1990-05-15").
118	- Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** unless a scenario says otherwise.
119	- "Narrow" is 360 × 740, "tablet" 768 × 1024, "desktop" 1280 × 800 CSS px.
120	- Copy in quotes that is not Strapi content is in §8.1.
121	
122	### US-04-AC-01 — Tokens in one file, no loose values (derived from US-04-BR-01)
123	
124	```gherkin
125	Scenario: Tokens in one file, no loose values
126	  Given the production style files of frontend/src
127	  Then exactly one file declares custom properties, in three tiers with distinct prefixes
128	  And no other style file contains a hex, rgb(), hsl(), oklch() or named colour, a px/rem/em length outside @media and @container conditions,
129	    a font-family name, a box-shadow or gradient literal, a ms/s duration, a cubic-bezier() or a numeric z-index
130	  And no component style file references a primitive token
131	  And every breakpoint used in a @media or @container condition is one of the breakpoints documented in the token file
132	```
133	
134	### US-04-AC-02 — AA contrast of the token pairs (derived from US-04-BR-02)
135	
136	```gherkin
137	Scenario Outline: AA contrast of the token pairs
138	  Given the token file declares the pair <foreground> on <background> as used in the UI
139	  When the WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio is computed (at every stop of a gradient background, and against the dotted texture composited at its opacity)
140	  Then the ratio is at least <minimum>
141	
142	  Examples:
143	    | foreground                         | background                               | minimum |
144	    | body text                          | page background                          | 4.5     |
145	    | muted text (help, captions)        | page background and card surface         | 4.5     |
146	    | error text                         | page background and card surface         | 4.5     |
147	    | primary button text                | primary button background (every stop)   | 4.5     |
148	    | text on the recommended card       | recommended card gradient (every stop)   | 4.5     |
149	    | display heading gradient text      | page background (every stop)             | 3       |
150	    | focus indicator                    | page background and card surface         | 3       |
151	    | input and card border              | page background and card surface         | 3       |
152	    | country accent (each country)      | page background and header surface       | 3       |
153	```
154	
155	The list of pairs is declared next to the tokens (format set by the ADR) so the test reads it
156	rather than guessing. Display headings meet 3:1 only if they are large text (BR-02).
157	
158	### US-04-AC-03 — Flags and country context (derived from US-04-BR-03 / Q-02, Q-10)
159	
160	```gherkin
161	Scenario Outline: Flags and country context
162	  When I open <page>
163	  Then I see the flag of <country> next to the text "<country>"
164	  And the flag is hidden from assistive technology, is not focusable and has no text content
165	  And <accessible check>
166	
167	  Examples:
168	    | page            | country  | accessible check |
169	    | "/"             | Colombia | the link's accessible name is exactly "Colombia" |
170	    | "/"             | Chile    | the link's accessible name is exactly "Chile" |
171	    | "/co/datos"     | Colombia | the wizard header shows "Colombia" as text and the page has one h1 |
172	    | "/cl/planes"    | Chile    | the wizard header shows "Chile" as text and the page has one h1 |
173	
174	Scenario: A country without front-end visuals
175	  Given a published country "Perú" with code "PE" exists only in Strapi
176	  When the country chooser is shown
177	  Then "Perú" is shown with the neutral globe icon and the brand accent, and no error
178	```
179

# US-04 — Design system and visual redesign · Spec

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story | [story.md](story.md) (English translation of the human's request, not edited; the human confirms the translation at HC1) |
| Status | Draft — awaiting HC1 |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Author | spec-writer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) |
| Approved by | — (human only, see Review log) |
| Related ADRs | [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (no country code in front-end code: conflicts with per-country flags and accents, US-04-Q-02), [ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) (stored values unchanged), [ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-forms-library.md) (custom select and date picker plug into Signal Forms and the shared validation core), [ADR-0009](../../adr/0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) (heading hierarchy). New ADRs needed: §10. |

Sources cited in this spec:

- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
- **US-01** [spec](../US-01/spec.md) v0.5 (Approved): field types, reserved keys, BR-01 (unreadable input is invalid), BR-02 (select prompt), BR-04 (`minAge`), AC-09 note (badInput semantics), AC-10 (error timing, focus), AC-24/25/26, Q-22 (native date input), §8.1 copy, §9 ("Native controls are used"); seed in [seed-fields.md](../US-01/seed-fields.md).
- **US-02** [spec](../US-02/spec.md) and **US-03** [spec](../US-03/spec.md) (Approved): plan cards as native radios, "Recomendado", summary sections, terms region, simulation radio group, focus order (US-02-AC-16, US-03-AC-16), §8.1 copy.
- **Existing tests**: `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts` (7 files) and `frontend/e2e/support/*.ts`; component tests and helpers in `frontend/src/**` (`testing/dom.ts`, `quote-form-page.spec.ts`, `static-guards.spec.ts`).
- **Evidence**: [docs/qa/US-04/README.md](../../docs/qa/US-04/README.md) (`before/` set; native popups not capturable).
- **Visual direction** given by the human with the brief (reference screenshot, inspiration only): dark near-black background with a subtle dotted texture; violet/indigo accent; recommended card with a violet vertical gradient and soft glow; rounded cards with thin borders; pill-shaped segmented toggles; check-circle icons in feature lists; large bold display headings with a soft text gradient; high-contrast white primary buttons.

## 1. Summary

A visual redesign of the whole quoting wizard (country chooser, step 1 form, plan list, summary,
payment and confirmation) on a tokenized design system, for people in Colombia and Chile on
phone, tablet and desktop. It adds country flags and a per-country accent, icons, an accessible
custom select and date picker (replacing the browser's native ones), a step indicator, step
transitions, skeletons and micro-animations that all honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, a
mobile-first responsive layout with 44 × 44 px targets, and self-hosted typography. Behaviour,
validation, stored values, routes and the Strapi contracts do not change; the existing tests keep
passing with the same strength, adapted only where a native element is replaced (§11.1).

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- A token file (primitive → semantic → component) and the restyling of every existing page and
  shared component through tokens only.
- Theme, palette, gradients, dotted background texture, type scale, two font families
  self-hosted (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08).
- Flags of CO and CL as SVG on the country chooser and in a new wizard header; per-country accent
  token (US-04-Q-02, Q-10).
- One icon library; icons inside step 1 inputs (by field key, with a default), in the step
  indicator, plan cards (check-circle in coverage and benefit lists), help, error and success
  messages (US-04-Q-09).
- Custom select (with search for long lists) and custom date picker (typed entry, calendar with
  month and year navigation, `minAge`-disabled days), built on accessible primitives, bound to the
  existing Signal Forms model (ADR-0004), with bottom sheet on mobile (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11,
  Q-12, Q-13).
- New interface microcopy owned by the front end (§8.1).
- Step indicator, step enter transition, hover/focus/active/disabled states, soft validation
  feedback, skeletons, interactive plan cards, summary and confirmation micro-animations
  (US-04-Q-14..Q-17).
- `prefers-reduced-motion`, responsive layout at 360 × 740, 768 × 1024 and 1280 × 800.
- Adapting existing tests where a native element is replaced, as listed in §11.1, and new tests.
- After screenshots in `docs/qa/US-04/after/` (US-04-Q-19).

**Out of scope**

- Any change to routes, guards, the wizard state, validation rules or messages, prices, masking,
  payment simulation, or the Strapi schema, seed, permissions and proxy (story: "Logic, the
  contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change").
- Rewriting help texts, placeholders or error messages that come from Strapi (US-04-Q-07).
- A light theme or a theme switch, unless US-04-Q-01 says otherwise.
- An in-wizard country switcher (US-01-Q-02 stands).
- Changing the native `number`, `text`, `checkbox` and `radio` controls into custom widgets; they
  are restyled only.
- Logos, names, slogans or texts of any real insurer or company; a brand name for the product.
- Adoption of the third-party design skills `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`: they
  are evaluated separately (task US-04-T-01); this spec does not rely on them.

## 3. Glossary

Terms of the US-01..US-03 glossaries keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Token | A CSS custom property declared in the single token file (BR-01). |
| Primitive / semantic / component token | Raw values (`--primitive-violet-500`), roles (`--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`), and per-component bindings (`--button-primary-bg`). Components use semantic or component tokens only. |
| Loose value | A literal colour, length, font, shadow, gradient, duration, easing or z-index in a component style instead of a `var(--…)` (allowed literals in BR-01). |
| Country accent | The per-country accent colour token, set from the current country context (BR-03). |
| Custom select | The design-system replacement for a `select` field: a WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup (BR-05). |
| Searchable select | A custom select whose option count reaches the search threshold; typing filters the options (US-04-Q-11). |
| Date field | The design-system replacement for a `date` field: a text box for typed entry plus an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (BR-06). |
| Calendar | The WAI-ARIA date picker dialog opened from the date field. |
| Shown value | What a control displays: the option label of a custom select (the prompt "Selecciona una opción" when empty), the dd/mm/aaaa text of a date field. |
| Stored value | The value in the editing model and in the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003, ADR-0004): option `value`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `''`. Unchanged by US-04. |
| Panel | The popup of a custom select or the calendar: an anchored popover on wide screens, a bottom sheet on narrow screens (US-04-Q-13). |
| Wizard header | New top bar on the wizard pages with the product name and the country chip (flag + country name). |
| Step indicator | New progress display of the three wizard steps (US-04-Q-17). |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

The story has no Gherkin scenarios, so every AC is derived. Conventions:

- "I completed step 1 in Colombia / Chile" uses the values of US-01-AC-04 / US-02 §5 conventions;
  the date is typed as "15/05/1990" (stored "1990-05-15").
- Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** unless a scenario says otherwise.
- "Narrow" is 360 × 740, "tablet" 768 × 1024, "desktop" 1280 × 800 CSS px.
- Copy in quotes that is not Strapi content is in §8.1.

# US-04 – Design system and visual redesign

## Story

As the product owner, I want a visual redesign built on a tokenized design system, so that the quoting
wizard is pleasant, consistent and accessible in Colombia and Chile, on mobile, tablet and desktop.

## How it is delivered

Treated as one more story of the flow: spec → ADR → tests → implementation → review → HC3.

Visual references are provided by the human as style inspiration (composition, density, tone). Do not
copy brands, logos, names or texts of any real insurer.

## Third-party design skills

- The human has `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable` and `frontend-design` installed globally. Evaluate them
  as `angular-developer` was evaluated: review their content and decide ADOPT / ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS /
  REJECT. If adopted, vendor them inside `.claude/skills/` with their entries in `THIRD_PARTY.md` and
  `docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`. Do not use the global copies directly. Wait for the human's
  decision before using them.
- Precedence as always: CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > project skills > third-party skills.

## Scope of the redesign

- **Tokens** as CSS custom properties in a single source file (color, typography, spacing, radii,
  shadows, gradients, animation durations and easing curves, z-index). Primitive → semantic →
  component tokens. No loose values in components.
- **Flags** of Colombia and Chile in SVG (a licensed library or our own optimized SVGs), visible in the
  country selector/context and in the wizard header. A per-country accent color through tokens. The
  flag is decorative next to the country name (`aria-hidden`), never the only indicator.
- **Subtle gradients** in backgrounds, headers and the primary button, making sure the text on top
  meets WCAG AA contrast.
- **Icons:** a single library with SVG icons imported individually (propose `lucide-angular` or
  another, with license and exact version). Add icons where they help the experience: inside the
  inputs (document, name, date, city, plate, make, model, year), in the wizard steps, in the plans, in
  help, error and success messages. The input icon comes from a front-end mapping by field key, with a
  generic default icon for new fields that arrive from Strapi. Decorative icons `aria-hidden`; icons
  that carry meaning have a label.
- **Custom select and calendar** (not the browser's native ones):
  - Select: our own dropdown in the design system's style, with an icon, search when the list is long
    (e.g. cities, makes), and the selected option marked.
  - Calendar (birth date): our own date picker with month navigation and fast year navigation (a year
    selector, because it is a birth date), days disabled according to the rules (minAge), and the date
    can also be typed by hand.
  - Built on accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or
    `@angular/aria` if it is stable in our version. Justify it in the ADR.
  - Full accessibility per the WAI-ARIA patterns (combobox/listbox and date picker dialog): arrows,
    Enter, Escape, Home/End, focus trapped and returned on close, screen-reader announcements.
  - On mobile the panel opens as a bottom sheet or full screen, comfortable to tap.
  - Validations and the stored value do not change; keyboard tests are added for both components.
- **Supporting text:** clear microcopy in help texts, placeholders, empty states and errors, so the
  experience is pleasant. Business content keeps coming from Strapi; only interface texts live in the
  front end.
- **Interactions and animation:** an animated wizard step indicator, transition between steps,
  hover/focus/active/disabled states, validation with soft feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, plan
  selection with interactive cards, and a summary with micro-animations. Propose the library in the ADR
  (for example Angular's native `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` with CSS, or Motion/GSAP if it really
  adds value) and justify bundle weight and maintenance.
- Everything honors **`prefers-reduced-motion`**: no movement if the user asks for it.
- **Responsive, mobile-first:** it must look good and be usable on phone, tablet and desktop (at least
  360×740, 768×1024 and 1280×800), with no horizontal scroll, touch targets of at least 44×44 px, and a
  layout that reorganizes (for example, plans in a column on mobile and in a grid on desktop).
- **Typography:** at most 2 families, loaded efficiently.

## Rules that do not change

- Logic, the contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change; it is a visual
  change. The existing e2e tests must keep passing without being loosened; if a selector changes, it is
  adjusted using accessible roles/labels, not CSS classes.
- Accessibility: visible focus everywhere, tab order intact, AA contrast, heading hierarchy per
  ADR-0009.
- Exact versions of any new dependency, license reviewed.
- Evidence in `docs/qa/US-04/`: before/after screenshots of CO and CL at the three sizes, for every
  wizard step, including the select and the calendar open.

## First deliverable

The evaluation of the skills and a short proposal (spec + design-system ADR, with an example palette
and type scale). Wait for the human's approval (HC1/HC2) before implementing.

1	# US-04 — Design system and visual redesign · Spec
2

New ADRs needed: §10. |
11	
12	Sources cited in this spec:
13	
14	- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
15	- **US-01** [spec](../US-01/spec.md) v0.5 (Approved): field types, reserved keys, BR-01 (unreadable input is invalid), BR-02 (select prompt), BR-04 (`minAge`), AC-09 note (badInput semantics), AC-10 (error timing, focus), AC-24/25/26, Q-22 (native date input), §8.1 copy, §9 ("Native controls are used"); seed in [seed-fields.md](../US-01/seed-fields.md).
16	- **US-02** [spec](../US-02/spec.md) and **US-03** [spec](../US-03/spec.md) (Approved): plan cards as native radios, "Recomendado", summary sections, terms region, simulation radio group, focus order (US-02-AC-16, US-03-AC-16), §8.1 copy.
17	- **Existing tests**: `frontend/e2e/*.spec.ts` (7 files) and `frontend/e2e/support/*.ts`; component tests and helpers in `frontend/src/**` (`testing/dom.ts`, `quote-form-page.spec.ts`, `static-guards.spec.ts`).
18	- **Evidence**: [docs/qa/US-04/README.md](../../docs/qa/US-04/README.md) (`before/` set; native popups not capturable).
19	- **Visual direction** given by the human with the brief (reference screenshot, inspiration only): dark near-black background with a subtle dotted texture; violet/indigo accent; recommended card with a violet vertical gradient and soft glow; rounded cards with thin borders; pill-shaped segmented toggles; check-circle icons in feature lists; large bold display headings with a soft text gradient; high-contrast white primary buttons.
20	
21	## 1. Summary
22	
23	A visual redesign of the whole quoting wizard (country chooser, step 1 form, plan list, summary,
24	payment and confirmation) on a tokenized design system, for people in Colombia and Chile on
25	phone, tablet and desktop. It adds country flags and a per-country accent, icons, an accessible
26	custom select and date picker (replacing the browser's native ones), a step indicator, step
27	transitions, skeletons and micro-animations that all honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, a
28	mobile-first responsive layout with 44 × 44 px targets, and self-hosted typography. Behaviour,
29	validation, stored values, routes and the Strapi contracts do not change; the existing tests keep
30	passing with the same strength, adapted only where a native element is replaced (§11.1).
31	
32	## 2. Scope
33	
34	**In scope**
35	
36	- A token file (primitive → semantic → component) and the restyling of every existing page and
37	  shared component through tokens only.
38	- Theme, palette, gradients, dotted background texture, type scale, two font families
39	  self-hosted (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08).
40	- Flags of CO and CL as SVG on the country chooser and in a new wizard header; per-country accent
41	  token (US-04-Q-02, Q-10).
42	- One icon library; icons inside step 1 inputs (by field key, with a default), in the step
43	  indicator, plan cards (check-circle in coverage and benefit lists), help, error and success
44	  messages (US-04-Q-09).
45	- Custom select (with search for long lists) and custom date picker (typed entry, calendar with
46	  month and year navigation, `minAge`-disabled days), built on accessible primitives, bound to the
47	  existing Signal Forms model (ADR-0004), with bottom sheet on mobile (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11,
48	  Q-12, Q-13).
49	- New interface microcopy owned by the front end (§8.1).
50	- Step indicator, step enter transition, hover/focus/active/disabled states, soft validation
51	  feedback, skeletons, interactive plan cards, summary and confirmation micro-animations
52	  (US-04-Q-14..Q-17).
53	- `prefers-reduced-motion`, responsive layout at 360 × 740, 768 × 1024 and 1280 × 800.
54	- Adapting existing tests where a native element is replaced, as listed in §11.1, and new tests.
55	- After screenshots in `docs/qa/US-04/after/` (US-04-Q-19).
56	
57	**Out of scope**
58	
59	- Any change to routes, guards, the wizard state, validation rules or messages, prices, masking,
60	  payment simulation, or the Strapi schema, seed, permissions and proxy (story: "Logic, the
61	  contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change").
62	- Rewriting help texts, placeholders or error messages that come from Strapi (US-04-Q-07).
63	- A light theme or a theme switch, unless US-04-Q-01 says otherwise.
64	- An in-wizard country switcher (US-01-Q-02 stands).
65	- Changing the native `number`, `text`, `checkbox` and `radio` controls into custom widgets; they
66	  are restyled only.
67	- Logos, names, slogans or texts of any real insurer or company; a brand name for the product.
68	- Adoption of the third-party design skills `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable`, `frontend-design`: they
69	  are evaluated separately (task US-04-T-01); this spec does not rely on them.
70	
71	## 3. Glossary
72	
73	Terms of the US-01..US-03 glossaries keep their meaning.
74	
75	| Term | Meaning in this project |
76	|---|---|
77	| Token | A CSS custom property declared in the single token file (BR-01). |
78	| Primitive / semantic / component token | Raw values (`--primitive-violet-500`), roles (`--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`), and per-component bindings (`--button-primary-bg`). Components use semantic or component tokens only. |
79	| Loose value | A literal colour, length, font, shadow, gradient, duration, easing or z-index in a component style instead of a `var(--…)` (allowed literals in BR-01). |
80	| Country accent | The per-country accent colour token, set from the current country context (BR-03). |
81	| Custom select | The design-system replacement for a `select` field: a WAI-ARIA combobox with a listbox popup (BR-05). |
82	| Searchable select | A custom select whose option count reaches the search threshold; typing filters the options (US-04-Q-11). |
83	| Date field | The design-system replacement for a `date` field: a text box for typed entry plus an "Elegir fecha" button that opens the calendar (BR-06). |
84	| Calendar | The WAI-ARIA date picker dialog opened from the date field. |
85	| Shown value | What a control displays: the option label of a custom select (the prompt "Selecciona una opción" when empty), the dd/mm/aaaa text of a date field. |
86	| Stored value | The value in the editing model and in the `quote-wizard` entry (ADR-0003, ADR-0004): option `value`, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `''`. Unchanged by US-04. |
87	| Panel | The popup of a custom select or the calendar: an anchored popover on wide screens, a bottom sheet on narrow screens (US-04-Q-13). |
88	| Wizard header | New top bar on the wizard pages with the product name and the country chip (flag + country name). |
89	| Step indicator | New progress display of the three wizard steps (US-04-Q-17). |
90	
91	## 4. Business rules
92	
93	| ID | Original (story) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
94	|---|---|---|---|
95	| US-04-BR-01 | "Tokens as CSS custom properties in a single source file (color, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, gradients, animation durations and easing curves, z-index). Primitive → semantic → component tokens. 16	# US-04 – Design system and visual redesign
17	
18	## Story
19	
20	As the product owner, I want a visual redesign built on a tokenized design system, so that the quoting
21	wizard is pleasant, consistent and accessible in Colombia and Chile, on mobile, tablet and desktop.
22	
23	## How it is delivered
24	
25	Treated as one more story of the flow: spec → ADR → tests → implementation → review → HC3.
26	
27	Visual references are provided by the human as style inspiration (composition, density, tone). Do not
28	copy brands, logos, names or texts of any real insurer.
29	
30	## Third-party design skills
31	
32	- The human has `ui-ux-pro-max`, `impeccable` and `frontend-design` installed globally. Evaluate them
33	  as `angular-developer` was evaluated: review their content and decide ADOPT / ADOPT WITH ADJUSTMENTS /
34	  REJECT. If adopted, vendor them inside `.claude/skills/` with their entries in `THIRD_PARTY.md` and
35	  `docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`. Do not use the global copies directly. Wait for the human's
36	  decision before using them.
37	- Precedence as always: CLAUDE.md > accepted ADRs > project skills > third-party skills.
38	
39	## Scope of the redesign
40	
41	- **Tokens** as CSS custom properties in a single source file (color, typography, spacing, radii,
42	  shadows, gradients, animation durations and easing curves, z-index). Primitive → semantic →
43	  component tokens. No loose values in components.
44	- **Flags** of Colombia and Chile in SVG (a licensed library or our own optimized SVGs), visible in the
45	  country selector/context and in the wizard header. A per-country accent color through tokens. The
46	  flag is decorative next to the country name (`aria-hidden`), never the only indicator.
47	- **Subtle gradients** in backgrounds, headers and the primary button, making sure the text on top
48	  meets WCAG AA contrast.
49	- **Icons:** a single library with SVG icons imported individually (propose `lucide-angular` or
50	  another, with license and exact version). Add icons where they help the experience: inside the
51	  inputs (document, name, date, city, plate, make, model, year), in the wizard steps, in the plans, in
52	  help, error and success messages. The input icon comes from a front-end mapping by field key, with a
53	  generic default icon for new fields that arrive from Strapi. Decorative icons `aria-hidden`; icons
54	  that carry meaning have a label.
55	- **Custom select and calendar** (not the browser's native ones):
56	  - Select: our own dropdown in the design system's style, with an icon, search when the list is long
57	    (e.g. cities, makes), and the selected option marked.
58	  - Calendar (birth date): our own date picker with month navigation and fast year navigation (a year
59	    selector, because it is a birth date), days disabled according to the rules (minAge), and the date
60	    can also be typed by hand.
61	  - Built on accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or
62	    `@angular/aria` if it is stable in our version. Justify it in the ADR.
63	  - Full accessibility per the WAI-ARIA patterns (combobox/listbox and date picker dialog): arrows,
64	    Enter, Escape, Home/End, focus trapped and returned on close, screen-reader announcements.
65	  - On mobile the panel opens as a bottom sheet or full screen, comfortable to tap.
66	  - Validations and the stored value do not change; keyboard tests are added for both components.
67	- **Supporting text:** clear microcopy in help texts, placeholders, empty states and errors, so the
68	  experience is pleasant. Business content keeps coming from Strapi; only interface texts live in the
69	  front end.
70	- **Interactions and animation:** an animated wizard step indicator, transition between steps,
71	  hover/focus/active/disabled states, validation with soft feedback, skeletons while Strapi loads, plan
72	  selection with interactive cards, and a summary with micro-animations. Propose the library in the ADR
73	  (for example Angular's native `animate.enter`/`animate.leave` with CSS, or Motion/GSAP if it really
74	  adds value) and justify bundle weight and maintenance.
75	- Everything honors **`prefers-reduced-motion`**: no movement if the user asks for it.
76	- **Responsive, mobile-first:** it must look good and be usable on phone, tablet and desktop (at least
77	  360×740, 768×1024 and 1280×800), with no horizontal scroll, touch targets of at least 44×44 px, and a
78	  layout that reorganizes (for example, plans in a column on mobile and in a grid on desktop).
79	- **Typography:** at most 2 families, loaded efficiently.
80	
81	## Rules that do not change
82	
83	- Logic, the contracts with Strapi and the texts that come from Strapi do not change; it is a visual
84	  change. The existing e2e tests must keep passing without being loosened; if a selector changes, it is
85	  adjusted using accessible roles/labels, not CSS classes.
86	- Accessibility: visible focus everywhere, tab order intact, AA contrast, heading hierarchy per
87	  ADR-0009.
88	- Exact versions of any new dependency, license reviewed.
89	- Evidence in `docs/qa/US-04/`: before/after screenshots of CO and CL at the three sizes, for every
90	  wizard step, including the select and the calendar open.
91	
92	## First deliverable
93	
94	The evaluation of the skills and a short proposal (spec + design-system ADR, with an example palette
95	and type scale). Wait for the human's approval (HC1/HC2) before implementing.

published, formatting of prices and dates on the summary, masking, security of content access*
are unchanged by a visual story (BR-07). *Configuration change mid-flow*: icons fall back to the
default for new keys (AC-04), selects with more options become searchable (Q-11).

## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

### 7.1 Strapi

**No change.** US-04 reads the same content as US-01..US-03 (ADR-0001, ADR-0006). The country
`name` and `localeTag` already provided are enough for the header and the calendar names. If
US-04-Q-02 takes its alternative, this section gains the `country` attributes and the story
changes its "contracts do not change" rule; that needs the human's answer first.

### 7.2 Front-end presentation maps (code, not content)

| Map | Key | Value | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Field icon | field `key` | icon (names per US-04-Q-09, fixed by the ADR) for `documentType`, `documentNumber`, `fullName`, `birthDate`, `city`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear` | default icon for any other key of type `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`; none for `checkbox` |
| Country visuals | country `code` (per US-04-Q-02) | flag SVG, accent token values | globe icon, brand accent |

Both maps are presentation only: no behaviour, validation or copy depends on them.

## 8. UI states

| State | Trigger | What the user sees | Accessibility notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loading | Content request in flight (fields, plans, terms, countries) | Skeleton shapes in place of the content | Skeleton `aria-hidden`; existing loading text in the polite live region; container `aria-busy` as today |
| Error / empty | As in US-01..US-03 | Same copy, restyled with an error or info icon | Unchanged roles (`alert`, `status`), focus rules unchanged |
| Select collapsed | Default | Icon, shown value or prompt "Selecciona una opción", chevron | `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded="false"` |
| Select open | Activation, keys of AC-06 | Popover or bottom sheet with options, selected option checked | `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-activedescendant`, listbox labelled by the field label |
| Select searching | Typing in a searchable select | Filtered options or "No encontramos opciones para «…»." | Count announced politely |
| Calendar open | "Elegir fecha" | Month and year, "Elegir año", month arrows, grid, disabled days dimmed and struck | `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, focus trapped, page inert |
| Year selector | "Elegir año" | List of years, current year marked | Listbox; Enter chooses and returns to the grid |
| Field invalid | Blur or failed "Continuar" | Message with error icon, soft fade-in, error border | Unchanged: `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, announced once |
| Hover / active / disabled | Pointer, press, `disabled` / `aria-disabled` | Distinct styles per control, from component tokens | Disabled style perceivable without colour only (opacity + cursor + icon or text where already present) |
| Plan chosen | Radio checked or card click | Violet border and glow, "Seleccionado" badge | Native radio state unchanged |
| Step change | "Continuar", "Atrás", back actions | Arriving page fades and rises in; indicator fill moves | Focus on the arriving `h1` (unchanged) |
| Processing payment | "Pagar" | Spinner in the button, "Procesando pago…" | Unchanged (US-03) |
| Confirmation | Payment approved | Check-circle draws in; indicator all completed | Unchanged focus and title |
| Reduced motion | `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` | Every state above without movement | — |

### 8.1 Code-owned copy added by US-04

Spanish, the same for both countries; extends US-01/US-02/US-03 §8.1. Existing strings are
reused unchanged ("Selecciona una opción", "Cotizador de seguro de auto", loading texts).

| String | Where |
|---|---|
| "No encontramos opciones para «{texto}»." | Searchable select, no match |
| "1 opción" / "{n} opciones" | Search result count (polite live region, visually hidden) |
| "Escribe para buscar" | Placeholder of a searchable select while open and empty |
| "Cerrar" | Close button of a bottom sheet and of the calendar |
| "Elegir fecha" | Calendar button next to each date field (accessible name "Elegir fecha: {label}") |
| "dd/mm/aaaa" | Placeholder of the date text box |
| "Formato: dd/mm/aaaa" | Hint under the date text box, in its accessible description |
| "Elegir año" / "Mes anterior" / "Mes siguiente" | Calendar controls |
| "Tus datos" / "Plan" / "Resumen y pago" | Step indicator labels |
| "Progreso de la cotización" | Accessible name of the step indicator list |
| "Paso {n} de 3" / "completado" | Visually hidden step indicator texts |

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA; WAI-ARIA APG combobox (select-only and list autocomplete) and
  date picker dialog patterns; visible focus on the focused element; Tab order unchanged except the
  "Elegir fecha" stop; one `h1` per page; decorative icons and flags hidden; `forced-colors`
  fallbacks for gradient text and borders; screen reader pass at HC3 (NVDA or VoiceOver) on the
  select, the calendar and the step indicator.
- **Responsive:** mobile-first CSS; 320–1440 CSS px with no horizontal scroll (verified at 360,
  768, 1280); 44 × 44 px targets; bottom sheet below 600 px.
- **Multi-country:** one build; no country branch except the presentation map of US-04-Q-02;
  calendar names and date formatting from `Intl` and the country `localeTag`; the date text format
  is the same for every country.
- **Security / privacy:** no third-party origin at runtime (fonts, icons, flags self-hosted, so no
  new CSP or proxy change); no value of the form in logs; no `innerHTML` for icons or flags (the
  existing static guard applies: icons and flags are components or inline template SVG).
- **Performance:** icons imported individually; fonts subset WOFF2, at most the weights used;
  the production build stays within the existing `angular.json` budgets (initial 500 kB warning,
  1 MB error; component styles 4 kB warning, 8 kB error), or the ADR justifies a change; no
  animation runs on layout properties (transform and opacity only).
- **Maintainability:** tokens in one file; new shared components under `src/app/shared/`
  (CLAUDE.md §6 naming, for example `custom-select.ts` → `CustomSelect`, `date-field.ts` →
  `DateField`, `step-indicator.ts` → `StepIndicator`; final names by the ADR or the developer).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, docs English.

## 10. ADRs

- **Referenced (accepted, binding):**
  1. ADR-0001 — no country code in front-end code (conflict: US-04-Q-02); routes and focus on the
     arriving heading (unchanged).
  2. ADR-0003 — stored values and their shape unchanged (AC-11).
  3. ADR-0004 — Signal Forms over the shared validation core; string editing model; error timing;
     `focusBoundControl()` on a failed submit. The custom controls must plug into it (US-04-Q-04);
     the `syncNative` implementation note changes for dates.
  4. ADR-0009 — heading levels of the summary and terms (AC-20).
  5. ADR-0002 / ADR-0005 — proxy and access unchanged; nothing new is fetched from Strapi or from a
     third party.
- **Needed (for the architect; written in parallel to HC1):**
  1. **Design tokens and visual language** (US-04-Q-01, Q-03, Q-08, Q-09, Q-10): token tiers,
     prefixes and file; how "no loose values" is enforced (static guard test vs a linter such as
     Stylelint, pinned); theme; palette with a contrast table of every pair of AC-02 and the
     format the test reads; gradients and the dotted texture; type scale (sizes, weights, line
     heights) and the two families with source, subset, licence and loading; spacing, radii,
     shadows, z-index and breakpoint scales; icon library (exact version, licence, Angular 22
     compatibility, import style) and the field-key map; flags. Includes the example palette and
     type scale the story asks for as the first deliverable.
  2. **Country visuals vs ADR-0001** (US-04-Q-02): amend ADR-0001 for a presentation-only map keyed
     by country code with a neutral fallback, or extend the `country` content type. May be a
     section of ADR 1 if it explicitly amends ADR-0001 and updates its review grep.
  3. **Accessible custom select and date picker primitives and their ADR-0004 integration**
     (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13): `@angular/cdk` (Overlay, `cdk/listbox` or `ListKeyManager`,
     `cdk/a11y` FocusTrap and LiveAnnouncer) at an exact version compatible with 22.3.0, vs
     `@angular/aria` at 22.3.0 (verify stability: developer preview or stable, and which patterns
     it covers: combobox, listbox, grid); from scratch is excluded by the story. Must state: the
     labelable focus element; Signal Forms custom-control binding (`FormValueControl<string>` or
     equivalent) so `[formField]`, `touched`, `focusBoundControl()` and the existing `aria-*`
     bindings work; where the overlay is attached (inside the component vs `document.body`) and
     what that means for component-test queries; typed-date parsing as a pure function next to the
     validators, mapping unreadable text to `''`; reuse of the field validator for disabled days;
     bottom sheet vs popover. It amends ADR-0004's D7 ("native controls") for `select` and `date`
     and its `syncNative` implementation note for dates.
  4. **Motion** (US-04-Q-14, Q-16): native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` with CSS and duration
     and easing tokens vs router `withViewTransitions()` vs Motion or GSAP; bundle weight and
     maintenance; enter-only step transition; reduced-motion mechanism and how AC-17 measures it.

## 5. Third-party skill overrides

These rules override the vendored `angular-developer` skill (see
`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`, EVAL-001):

- **Forms strategy is not taken from the skill.** `references/signal-forms.md` says Signal Forms
  are mandatory; that is not binding. The forms strategy is **ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20,
  after SPIKE-01): Signal Forms over a shared, library-agnostic validation core. Where ADR-0004
  differs from the skill (for example, number fields hold strings in the model, not `0`), follow
  ADR-0004.
- **The Angular CLI MCP server is not used.** Do not configure it (`references/mcp.md`) and do
  not run `npx @angular/cli mcp`.
- **The Angular CLI version is pinned** (§4). The skill's "no version / `@latest`" defaults do
  not apply.
- **Naming follows §6**, not the skill's ambiguous examples.
- **Keyboard accessibility of the wizard** is enforced by the project `review-checklist` skill.
  The skill's ARIA guidance is supplementary.
- Reads of `angular.dev` are allowed as a reference, but any decision based on them must be
  written into a spec or ADR.
These rules override the vendored `frontend-design` skill (EVAL-005, human decision 2026-11-21):

- **No memory.** The skill says to use "information in your memory about the client" and to keep
  notes between passes. Use only the repository's artifacts (§3; story, spec, ADRs, `tasks.md`).
- **The brief is the approved spec and ADRs.** "Confirm with the client" means a spec question
  (`US-NN-Q-NN`) answered at HC1/HC2, never an assumption. The skill's own rule applies: the
  brief's words win, including when the approved direction matches one of the skill's "generated
  defaults" (for example a dark background with one accent, or cards with gradients).
- **No aesthetic risk beyond the accepted ADR.** The wizard is a task flow, not a landing page: no
  hero, no extra sections, no decoration the spec does not ask for. Accessibility, the
  `review-checklist` skill and the accepted ADRs come first.
- **Copy.** Only interface microcopy, in Spanish, code-owned (spec §8.1 of each story). Business
  content from Strapi is never rewritten or invented.
- Never edit vendored skill files. Overrides go here.

## 6. Naming conventions

decision-makers: <human name> (approval), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: <spike / agents / docs>
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence

What problem forces a decision now? Two to four sentences. Link the stories and specs:
US-XX, `specs/US-XX/spec.md#…`.

- …

2. <Option B>
3. <Option C>

Chosen option: "<Option X>", because <justification tied to the drivers>.

### Consequences

- Bad, because … — mitigation: …
- Neutral: …

### Strongest argument against

The single best argument against the chosen option, stated as a proponent of the best
alternative would state it. Do not soften it.

**Why we accept it:** the mitigation, or the reason the drivers still favour this option.

### Confirmation

How we verify that the implementation complies (test, review checklist item, script).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### <Option A>

<description or example>

- Good, because …
- Bad, because …

### <Option B>

- Good, because …
- Bad, because …

## More Information

- Related ADRs: …
- Revisit when: <condition that would reopen this decision>

1	---
2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, strapi-content-modeling skill, published packages @strapi/core, @strapi/i18n, @strapi/utils 5.63.0 and @angular/router 22.3.0

9	# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
14	fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
15	by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
16	item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
17	Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
18	countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
19	addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
24	- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
25	- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
26	- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
27	- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
28	- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
29	- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
30	- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
31	- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.
32	
33	## Considered Options
34	
35	Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):
36	
37	1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
38	2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
39	3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
40	4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).
41	
42	Country resolution in Angular:
43	
44	- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
45	- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
46	- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
47	- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.
48	
49	## Decision Outcome
50	
51	Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
52	is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
53	country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
54	explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.
55	
56	### What is decided
57	
58	**Strapi model**
59	
60	- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
61	  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
62	  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
63	  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
64	  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
65	  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
66	- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
67	  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
68	- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
69	  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
70	  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
71	  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
72	- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
73	  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
74	  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
75	  be used for this.
76	- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
77	  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
78	  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
79	  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
80	  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
81	  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.
82	
83	**Country context in Angular**
84	
85	- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
86	  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
87	  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
88	  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
89	  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
90	- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
91	  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
92	- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
93	  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
94	  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
95	- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
96	  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
97	- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
98	  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
99	  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
100	  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
101	- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
102	  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
103	  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
104	  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.
105	
106	**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**
107	
108	| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
109	|---|---|---|---|
110	| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
111	| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
112	| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
113	| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
114	| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
115	| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
116	| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
117	| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |
118	
119	- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
120	  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
121	- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
122	  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
123	  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
124	  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
125	  separate child routes.
126	- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
127	  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
128	  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
129	  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
130	  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
131	  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
132	  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
133	- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
134	  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
135	- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
136	  in their stories, spec §8).
137	- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
138	  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).
139	
140	### Consequences
141	
142	- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
143	  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
144	- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
145	- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
146	  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
147	  code-backed rules.
148	- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
149	  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
150	- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
151	  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
152	  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
153	- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
154	  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
155	  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
156	- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
157	  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
158	- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
159	  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
160	- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
161	  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
162	- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
163	  HC1, US-01-Q-27).
164	
165	### Strongest argument against
166	
167	Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
168	scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
169	editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
170	needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
171	editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
172	country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
173	list would not.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
176	in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
177	country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
178	metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
179	duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
180	surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".
181	
182	### Confirmation
183	
184	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
185	  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
186	  (AC-22).
187	- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
188	  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
189	  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
190	- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
191	  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
192	  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
193	- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).
194	
195	## Pros and Cons of the Options
196	
197	### A. `country` collection type + relation
198	
199	- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
200	- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
201	- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
202	- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
203	- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.
204	
205	### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)
206	
207	Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).
208	
209	- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
210	  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
211	  per country with no custom code.
212	- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
213	- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
214	  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
215	  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
216	  price.
217	- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
218	  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
219	- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
220	  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.
221	
222	### C. Enumeration attribute `country`
223	
224	- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
225	- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
226	- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
227	  which BR-07 forbids.
228	
229	### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)
230	
231	- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
232	- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
233	  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
234	  without an extra flag).
235	- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
236	  error-prone for non-technical editors.
237	
238	### R1. Path segment (chosen)
239	
240	- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
241	- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
242	- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
243	  the other country's data).
244	
245	### R2. Host name
246	
247	- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
248	- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
249	  single-command start (Assessment, environment).
250	
251	### R3. Query parameter
252	
253	- Good, because it needs no routing change.
254	- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
255	  for guards and tests.
256	
257	### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser
258	
259	- Good, because URLs stay short.
260	- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
261	  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.
262	
263	## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)
264	
265	1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
266	   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
267	2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
268	   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
269	3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.
270	
271	## More Information
272	
273	- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
274	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
275	  (files cited inline).
276	- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
277	  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
278	- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
279	  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).
- Bad, because there is no editor tool to copy the CO form to CL (i18n would offer "fill from
  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

### Strongest argument against

Option B (i18n locales `es-CO` / `es-CL`) gives per-country `key` uniqueness for free: Strapi
scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets
editors fill one country's content from another's. Option A gives up both: uniqueness per country
needs custom server code that we must write, test and keep working across Strapi upgrades, and
editors have no tool to copy the CO form to CL. Making the country list content also means the
country chooser and the unknown-country page depend on Strapi being reachable, where a hard-coded
list would not.

**Why we accept it:** option B copies non-localised attributes to every locale on save (verified
in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other
country's value; it mixes language with market and still needs a second mechanism for country
metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops
duplicates (AC-14), copying is a minor cost with two countries, and the Strapi dependency is
surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
  (AC-22).
- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.

### B. i18n locales as countries (`es-CO`, `es-CL`)

Both locales exist in Strapi's ISO list (`@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `constants/iso-locales.json.js`).

- Good, because Strapi scopes `unique` by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
  per country with no custom code.
- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
  price.
- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

### C. Enumeration attribute `country`

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name

- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
  single-command start (Assessment, environment).

### R3. Query parameter

- Good, because it needs no routing change.
- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
  for guards and tests.

### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser

- Good, because URLs stay short.
- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. Spec §7.3 types `country` as `'CO' | 'CL'`. With a content-driven country list it becomes an
   ISO alpha-2 code validated against the loaded countries.
2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).
3. AC-17's links come from Strapi; they are absent while the load error is shown.

## More Information

- Verified sources (all on 2026-11-20, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (files cited inline).
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (who may read `country` and `form-field`, and how), ADR-0003 (wizard state
  scope per country and clearing on switch), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved).
- Revisit when: a country needs more than one language, a country needs code-backed rules that
  content cannot express, or the business needs to copy whole forms between countries often.
