| Panel close | instant by default; `animate.leave` only if the developer confirms it runs when the CDK overlay detaches (no AC needs it) | opacity |
| Error text | `animate.enter="error-enter"` | opacity only (no shake); the text is in the DOM, inside `role="alert"`, from the first frame (D6) |
| Hover / active / chosen plan | CSS transitions | `border-color`, `box-shadow`, `background-color` (paint), and a 2 px lift on hover only for `(hover: hover)` pointers |
| Skeleton shimmer | keyframes on a pseudo-element | `transform: translateX()` |
| "Pagar" spinner | keyframes on the icon | `transform: rotate()` |
| Summary sections | `animate.enter` with `--delay-stagger-n` by `:nth-of-type` | opacity, translateY |
| Confirmation | `animate.enter` on the check-circle | scale 0.85 → 1 and opacity, `--duration-slow` (the single orchestrated moment of the flow) |

Not animated: prices and numbers (no counting up, D6), headings, the country chooser list, text in
live regions. Hover transitions are colour and shadow changes, not motion, except the 2 px lift
(D7: "hover transitions on every card" read as generated; the plan cards are the one place where a
lift explains "this is clickable", US-04-BR-09).

**Step transition, why one page only.** The router removes the leaving component and inserts the
arriving one in the same change; with no `animate.leave`, Angular does not keep the old element.
Only the arriving page animates in, so there is never a second `h1` or `main` (AC-14). Focus moves
to the arriving `h1` as today: opacity and transform do not affect focus or the accessibility tree.

#### 3. Reduced motion, by construction (D1)

- In every style file except `tokens.css`, each `animation`, `animation-*`, `transition` and
  `transition-*` declaration sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { … }`.
  Under `reduce` no animation or transition is declared at all: computed durations are the initial
  `0s`, `document.getAnimations()` is empty, and states (colour, border, icon, text) still change,
  instantly. This keeps feedback while removing movement, a principle restated from
  `pbakaus/impeccable` `animate.md` (Apache-2.0, credited per EVAL-004), and it avoids the global
  `0.01ms !important` kill switch that the same source flags.
- `animate.enter` classes therefore have no animation under `reduce`; Angular reads the computed
  styles, finds none, and removes the class at once (`@angular/core@22.3.0`
  `determineLongestAnimation` falls back to computed styles when `getAnimations()` is empty;
  `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` default 4000 ms is never reached).
- The duration tokens are also set to `0ms` under `reduce` in `tokens.css`, so a declaration that
  escapes the `no-preference` block still has no duration.
- **CDK overlays and dialogs** (ADR-0012) are created with `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK's own
  backdrop has `transition: opacity 400ms` and, under reduced motion, `transition-duration: 1ms`
  (`@angular/cdk@22.3.0` overlay styles), which would fail AC-17's "0s"; with
  `disableAnimations`, the CDK adds `cdk-overlay-backdrop-noop-animation` (`transition: none`). Our
  own backdrop fade, if any, is a token transition inside the `no-preference` block in
  `styles.css`.
- The spinner stops under `reduce`; "Procesando pago…" (US-03) remains the feedback.

#### 4. Tests (AC-14, AC-17)

- **Static guard** (extends ADR-0010's guard): outside `tokens.css`, no `animation`/`transition`
  declaration outside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block; durations, delays and
  easings only as `var(--duration-*)`, `var(--delay-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`; `tokens.css` sets every
  `--duration-*` and `--delay-*` to `0ms` under `reduce`; every `createOverlayRef`,
  `cdkConnectedOverlay` and `Dialog.open` call passes `disableAnimations: true` (a grep on the
  production sources).
- **E2E AC-17**: a Playwright context with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` walks step 1 (with "Ciudad"
  open and the calendar open), step 2, the summary and the confirmation; on each state it asserts
  that every element's computed `animationDuration` and `transitionDuration` list only `0s`, and
  `document.getAnimations()` is empty.
- **E2E AC-14**: with motion allowed, a `MutationObserver` installed before "Continuar" records the
  maximum number of `h1` and `main` elements seen during navigation (expected 1 and 1); then focus
  is on "Elige tu plan" and the title is unchanged; the page's enter animation reports a duration
  ≤ `--duration-slow` through `getAnimations()`.

### Consequences

- Good, because no dependency, no bytes, no licence question (D3); `animate.enter` is
  `@publicApi 20.2` in `@angular/core@22.3.0` and the vendored skill's own guidance for v20.2+.
- Good, because reduced motion is a property of how styles are written, enforced by a guard, not a
  late override that can be missed (D1).
- Good, because one page is ever in the DOM (D2), and focus and announcements are untouched (D6).
- Bad, because the old page disappears without an exit animation, so the change is a cut followed by
  a fade-in, less fluid than a cross-fade — mitigation: the fade is short (200 ms) and the step
  indicator fill gives continuity; B can be added later as an enhancement if the human wants a
  cross-fade (see *Revisit*).
- Bad, because closing a panel inside a CDK overlay may not run `animate.leave` (the overlay detaches
  its content) — mitigation: panels close instantly unless the developer proves the leave runs; no
  AC requires a close animation.
- Bad, because writing every animation inside a media block is a discipline — mitigation: the guard
  fails the gate otherwise.
- Neutral: the first page load also plays `page-enter` once; that is the single page-load moment.

### Strongest argument against

The View Transitions route (B) gives a real two-state transition with one line,
`withViewTransitions()`: the browser snapshots the old page and cross-fades it into the new one,
while the live DOM still holds only the new page (so AC-14 holds too). It can even morph the step
indicator between steps with a `view-transition-name`, which is the "animated step indicator" the
story asks for, and browsers without support simply skip it. Enter-only CSS is a hard cut followed
by a fade, the kind of generic "fade-and-rise" the `frontend-design` skill calls a tell of generated
pages.

**Why we accept it:** B only animates route changes, so the panels, errors, skeletons, cards,
spinner and confirmation still need A: two mechanisms, two reduced-motion paths (B also needs
`skipTransition()` or `::view-transition-*` rules under `reduce`, and its pseudo-element
animations show up in `document.getAnimations()` during AC-17). `withViewTransitions` is tagged
`@publicApi 22.3` in the 22.3.0 typings, so it has been public API only since the release we pin,
three days before this ADR. The fade-in here is brief and paired with the indicator fill, and the
one orchestrated moment is the confirmation, as the skill advises. B stays a contained later
enhancement on top of A.

### Confirmation

- Static guard rules of §4 (US-04-AC-17, AC-01).
- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: AC-14 and AC-17 as in §4.
- Component tests (AC-15): skeletons are `aria-hidden`, the loading text stays in its live region.
- HC3: the human checks the motion with the OS setting on and off (AC-23).
- `frontend/package.json` contains no `motion`, `gsap`, `@angular/animations` or other animation
  dependency (dependency list guard of ADR-0010).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Native `animate.enter` / `animate.leave` + CSS (chosen)

- Good, because zero bytes and zero dependencies; stable API since 20.2.
- Good, because every effect is plain CSS on tokens, and reduced motion is enforced statically.
- Bad, because there is no exit for the leaving page (by design) and limited choreography.

### B. Router `withViewTransitions()`

`@angular/router@22.3.0` typings: `withViewTransitions` tagged `@publicApi 22.3`.

- Good, because a true cross-fade (or a morph of named elements) with one line; one page in the DOM.
- Good, because progressive: unsupported browsers navigate without a transition.
- Bad, because it covers route changes only; everything else still needs A.
- Bad, because reduced motion needs its own handling, and its animations appear in
  `document.getAnimations()` while running.
- Bad, because it became public API in 22.3.0 itself.

### C. Motion 14.14.0 or GSAP 3.15.1

Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `motion@14.14.0` MIT, unpacked 1.0 MB; `gsap@3.15.1` licence
"Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license", unpacked 6.3 MB. Measured on a
throwaway build (baseline initial 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `import { animate } from
'motion'` **+74.10 kB raw / +23.97 kB transfer**; `motion/mini` **+8.92 / +2.71**; `gsap`
**+71.36 / +25.00**.

- Good, because springs, timelines and sequencing beyond CSS.
- Bad, because nothing in the spec needs them: every listed effect is a CSS transform or opacity.
- Bad, because the weight is real (motion, gsap) or the features are what CSS already has
  (motion/mini); one more dependency to upgrade.
- Bad, because GSAP's licence is not an OSI permissive licence, so US-04-BR-14 would need a human
  exception.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. **US-04-Q-16** "confirmation check-circle draw": a stroke "draw" animates `stroke-dashoffset`,
   which is neither transform nor opacity (spec §9). This ADR uses a scale-and-fade instead. If the
   human wants the draw, spec §9 should allow paint-only SVG stroke properties.
2. **US-04-AC-01 / BR-01** allowed media conditions: the guard of ADR-0010 must also accept the
   `(hover: hover)` media feature used for the card lift.
3. **US-04-AC-17** "document.getAnimations() returns no running animation": with §3 it returns no
   animation at all; the scenario may assert the stronger "empty".

## More Information

- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (installed `frontend/node_modules`, packed `@angular/cdk@22.3.0`, npm
  registry, a throwaway build in a temporary directory; nothing installed in the project):
  - `@angular/core@22.3.0` typings: `AnimationCallbackEvent` and the `animate.enter`/`animate.leave`
    types are `@publicApi 20.2`; runtime in `fesm2022/_debug_node-chunk.mjs`
    (`determineLongestAnimation`, `MAX_ANIMATION_TIMEOUT` default 4000).
  - `@angular/router@22.3.0` typings: `withViewTransitions` `@publicApi 22.3`.
  - `@angular/cdk@22.3.0`: `OverlayConfig.disableAnimations`, `DialogConfig.disableAnimations`;
    overlay styles: backdrop `transition: opacity 400ms …`, reduced-motion `transition-duration: 1ms`,
    `.cdk-overlay-backdrop-noop-animation { transition: none }`.
  - Bundle numbers in *Pros and Cons* C.
- **Credit:** "reduce movement, keep feedback", "exits faster than entries", "no bounce by reflex",
  "animate transform and opacity" are restated from `pbakaus/impeccable` at `0a4e72a` (`animate.md`,
  Apache-2.0), as EVAL-004 allows.
- **Skill notes:** the vendored `angular-animations.md` recommends `animate.enter`/`animate.leave`
  for v20.2+ (consistent); `route-animations.md` describes `withViewTransitions` (option B, not
  chosen). `@angular/animations` is not added.
- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0010 (tokens, guard), ADR-0012 (CDK overlays and dialog), ADR-0001 (focus on
  the arriving heading).
- **Revisit when:** the human asks for a cross-fade between steps (add B on top of A, with its own
  reduced-motion handling and an AC-17 row), or a later story needs choreography CSS cannot express.

# Architecture Decision Records

Format: MADR 4 (see the `adr-madr` skill). Only a human sets an ADR to `Accepted` or `Rejected`.
Accepted ADRs are binding (`CLAUDE.md` §1, level 2) and are never rewritten; they are superseded.

## Index

| ADR | Title | Status | Date | Stories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) | Multi-country content strategy and country context (includes wizard routes and step guards) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0006) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0003](0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) | Front-end persistence of the wizard state | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0004](0004-forms-library.md) | Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form (Signal Forms over a shared validation core) | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01 |
| [0005](0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) | Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01 |
| [0006](0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) | Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01, US-02 |
| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |
| [0008](0008-simulated-payment.md) | Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0009](0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) | Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0002 | **Terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** ADR-0002 names the US-03 permission `api::terms.terms.find`. Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a content type whose singular and plural names are equal (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`, `validateContentTypesUnicity`: "The plural name … should be unique"), so the type is **`api::term.term`** (singularName `term`, pluralName `terms`, as in CLAUDE.md §6). Consequently: the public permission is **`api::term.term.find`** (no `findOne`), reconciled in bootstrap with the existing three; the router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object (US-01-R2-F03), so `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` covers it; the REST path stays **`/api/terms`**, which must be added to the GET-only allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template` (today `countries|form-fields|plans`). The decision (public `find` only, published-only reads, GET-only proxy, no write token in the browser) is unchanged. | US-03 spec v0.1 (US-03-Q-03, §7.4) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNative` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validity.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-24 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal Forms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05); US-01-R3-F02 |
| 0003 | **An empty wizard state is represented by no `quote-wizard` entry (US-03-R1-F02).** A state with no step 1 values and no chosen plan leaves no entry in `sessionStorage`. a3f186c added this to `QuoteStore.persist()` as an early `return`, which only skipped the write: an entry that already existed stayed, for example after `prune()` drops every stored key because none is configured any more, so the values of removed fields remained in the tab. b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) fixed it: for an empty state, `persist()` (`frontend/src/app/core/quote-store.ts:163-178`, empty branch `:169-172`) now **removes** any existing entry by calling `clearStorage()` (call on `:170`, method `:180-186`) and then returns, so the invariant "empty state ⇒ no entry" holds in every case, and ADR-0003's "the pruned state is written back" is met by removal when the pruned state is empty (`prune()`, `:88-98`). Consequences: entering a country with an empty step 1 (`enterCountry`, `:42-51`) no longer writes `{country, step1: {values: {}}}`, a change to US-01 behaviour; nothing is lost, because the country is always known from the `/:country` route, which calls `enterCountry` on each entry (ADR-0001), and the entry is written on the first value or plan choice. After a successful payment, `clearQuote()` (`:58-64`) removes the entry, and a reload, a back action or "Nueva cotización" re-enters the country with an empty state, so no entry is found (US-03-AC-11). The decision of ADR-0003 (one versioned `sessionStorage` entry per tab, scoped to one country, cleared on country change and on successful payment) is unchanged. | a3f186c; b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) |

## Backlog (decisions known to be needed)

Numbers are assigned when an ADR is written; this order is only provisional.

| Topic | Why it needs an ADR | Input |

| — | No pending ADR for US-01, US-02 or US-03 | — |

Covered since 2026-11-21 for US-03 (both Accepted at HC2 by the human, 2026-11-21): the simulated
payment (ADR-0008; US-03-Q-01) and the terms rich-text format and rendering (ADR-0009;
US-03-Q-02). The terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03) is an implementation note on ADR-0002 above.

Covered since 2026-11-21: the simulated price rule of US-02 (ADR-0007, Accepted: option A; US-02-Q-01) and
the summary route registered by US-02 (implementation note on ADR-0001 above; US-02-Q-03).

Covered since 2026-11-20: the multi-country content strategy (ADR-0001, which also folds in the
wizard routing and step guards candidate from US-01 spec §10), the Strapi access and security
model (ADR-0002), the front-end persistence of the wizard state (ADR-0003), and the forms library
(ADR-0004, informed by [SPIKE-01](../docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md)).

# Architecture Decision Records

Format: MADR 4 (see the `adr-madr` skill). Only a human sets an ADR to `Accepted` or `Rejected`.
Accepted ADRs are binding (`CLAUDE.md` §1, level 2) and are never rewritten; they are superseded.

## Index

| ADR | Title | Status | Date | Stories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) | Multi-country content strategy and country context (includes wizard routes and step guards) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0006) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0003](0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) | Front-end persistence of the wizard state | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0004](0004-forms-library.md) | Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form (Signal Forms over a shared validation core) | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01 |
| [0005](0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) | Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01 |
| [0006](0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) | Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01, US-02 |
| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |
| [0008](0008-simulated-payment.md) | Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0009](0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) | Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0010](0010-design-tokens-and-visual-language.md) | Design tokens and visual language: one token file in three tiers, static guard, dark theme, palette with contrast proof, Archivo + Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, `@lucide/angular`, own flag SVGs | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0011](0011-country-visuals-amends-adr-0001.md) | Country visuals (flag and accent) as a presentation-only front-end map (amends ADR-0001) | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0012](0012-accessible-select-and-date-picker.md) | Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004) | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0013](0013-motion-and-reduced-motion.md) | Motion with native `animate.enter` and CSS on duration tokens, enter-only step transition, reduced motion by construction | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0002 | **Terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** ADR-0002 names the US-03 permission `api::terms.terms.find`. Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a content type whose singular and plural names are equal (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`, `validateContentTypesUnicity`: "The plural name … should be unique"), so the type is **`api::term.term`** (singularName `term`, pluralName `terms`, as in CLAUDE.md §6). Consequently: the public permission is **`api::term.term.find`** (no `findOne`), reconciled in bootstrap with the existing three; the router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object (US-01-R2-F03), so `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` covers it; the REST path stays **`/api/terms`**, which must be added to the GET-only allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template` (today `countries|form-fields|plans`). The decision (public `find` only, published-only reads, GET-only proxy, no write token in the browser) is unchanged. | US-03 spec v0.1 (US-03-Q-03, §7.4) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNative` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validity.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-24 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal Forms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05); US-01-R3-F02 |
| 0003 | **An empty wizard state is represented by no `quote-wizard` entry (US-03-R1-F02).** A state with no step 1 values and no chosen plan leaves no entry in `sessionStorage`. a3f186c added this to `QuoteStore.persist()` as an early `return`, which only skipped the write: an entry that already existed stayed, for example after `prune()` drops every stored key because none is configured any more, so the values of removed fields remained in the tab. b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) fixed it: for an empty state, `persist()` (`frontend/src/app/core/quote-store.ts:163-178`, empty branch `:169-172`) now **removes** any existing entry by calling `clearStorage()` (call on `:170`, method `:180-186`) and then returns, so the invariant "empty state ⇒ no entry" holds in every case, and ADR-0003's "the pruned state is written back" is met by removal when the pruned state is empty (`prune()`, `:88-98`). Consequences: entering a country with an empty step 1 (`enterCountry`, `:42-51`) no longer writes `{country, step1: {values: {}}}`, a change to US-01 behaviour; nothing is lost, because the country is always known from the `/:country` route, which calls `enterCountry` on each entry (ADR-0001), and the entry is written on the first value or plan choice. After a successful payment, `clearQuote()` (`:58-64`) removes the entry, and a reload, a back action or "Nueva cotización" re-enters the country with an empty state, so no entry is found (US-03-AC-11). The decision of ADR-0003 (one versioned `sessionStorage` entry per tab, scoped to one country, cleared on country change and on successful payment) is unchanged. | a3f186c; b3fdd45 (US-03-R1-F02) |

## US-04 step 2: four ADRs written, all `Proposed`, ready for HC1 + HC2

I made no commits, pushes or branch switches, and did not edit `spec.md`. Changed files:
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0010-design-tokens-and-visual-language.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0011-country-visuals-amends-adr-0001.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0012-accessible-select-and-date-picker.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0013-motion-and-reduced-motion.md` (new)

- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/tasks.md`: Status set to "HC1 + HC2", T-02..T-05 marked done (Proposed), one Gate history row.

`git status` shows only those files plus the untracked `spec.md`. I measured bundle sizes on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` in the scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/build`); nothing was installed in the project.

---

### ADR-0010: Design tokens and visual language
- **Decision:**
  - **Token file:** `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` is the only file that may declare custom properties or `@font-face`. There are three tiers: `--primitive-*`, semantic (`--color-*`, `--space-*` and so on) and `--component-*`.
  - **Contrast pair list:** `frontend/src/styles/contrast-pairs.json`. The test resolves each token name in it from `tokens.css`, including every gradient stop and the texture's worst case.

The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Follow-up on ADR-0012 (now Accepted, 2026-11-21). At HC1 the human decided that the calendar's first day of the week follows the country locale from CLDR (Sunday for es-CO, Monday for es-CL), derived from the locale with no country code in the date picker. # Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.

## Ground it in the subject

If the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before – use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Structure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.

Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: brainstorm, explore, plan, critique, build, critique again

For calibration: AI-generated design right now clusters around three looks: (1) a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta accent; (2) a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent; (3) a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.

## US-04 step 2: four ADRs written, all `Proposed`, ready for HC1 + HC2

I made no commits, pushes or branch switches, and did not edit `spec.md`. Changed files:
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0010-design-tokens-and-visual-language.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0011-country-visuals-amends-adr-0001.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0012-accessible-select-and-date-picker.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0013-motion-and-reduced-motion.md` (new)
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/README.md`: four index rows plus a backlog note. The "amended by" wording on the ADR-0001 and ADR-0004 rows only changes after acceptance.
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/tasks.md`: Status set to "HC1 + HC2", T-02..T-05 marked done (Proposed), one Gate history row.

`git status` shows only those files plus the untracked `spec.md`. I measured bundle sizes on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` in the scratchpad (`.../scratchpad/build`); nothing was installed in the project.

---

### ADR-0010: Design tokens and visual language
- **Decision:**
  - **Token file:** `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` is the only file that may declare custom properties or `@font-face`. There are three tiers: `--primitive-*`, semantic (`--color-*`, `--space-*` and so on) and `--component-*`.
  - **Contrast pair list:** `frontend/src/styles/contrast-pairs.json`. The test resolves each token name in it from `tokens.css`, including every gradient stop and the texture's worst case.
  - **Enforcement:** a Vitest static guard (option A1) that also tests itself on deliberate violations, so it cannot pass by finding nothing.
  - **Theme:** dark only.
  - **Icons:** `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`.
  - **Fonts:** Archivo (display, with a width axis) and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (text), copied to `/fonts/` from npm, Latin subset only, `swap`, text face preloaded.
  - **Flags:** our own SVG components.
- **Options:**
  - No-loose-values check: A1 static guard vs A2 Stylelint 18.1.0 with `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` 1.13.0.
  - Theme: dark only vs dark and light.
  - Icons: `@lucide/angular` vs `@ng-icons` 36.1.0 vs `lucide-angular` 1.0.0.
  - Fonts: the chosen pair vs Atkinson only vs Sora/Space Grotesk + Inter.
- **Strongest argument against:** Stylelint is the standard tool, with a real CSS parser and editor feedback; a regex guard re-implements a parser badly.
- **Verified:**
  - `lucide-angular` (the name in the story) is deprecated ("use @lucide/angular"). Its peer range is Angular 13.x–21.x, and installing it against 22.3.0 fails with ERESOLVE (reproduced).
  - `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0: ISC, peer >=17, side-effect free, no `innerHTML`, adds `aria-hidden` automatically when there is no title.
  - `@ng-icons/core` uses `innerHTML` internally.
  - Font packages 5.3.0 are OFL-1.1. File sizes: Archivo width-axis 90,104 B, Atkinson 33,996 B. Copying the files through Angular `assets` was checked in a real build.
  - Bundle sizes (initial `main`, raw / transfer): baseline 381.44 / 98.94 kB. With 22 Lucide icons +78.24 / +4.20 kB; with `@ng-icons` +13.27 / +2.50 kB.

### ADR-0011: Country visuals, amends ADR-0001
- **Decision:** a presentation-only map in `shared/country-visuals.ts`. It maps an ISO code to a flag component and an accent key; the hex values stay in `tokens.css`. Any other published country gets a globe icon and the brand accent.
- **Options:** front-end map vs new attributes on the Strapi `country` type vs flag emoji with no accent.
- **Strongest argument against:** the Strapi option keeps ADR-0001 intact and lets marketing add visuals for a new market with no release.
- **Amendment to ADR-0001:** an explicit, narrow exception to "No country code, name or list exists in front-end code". The review grep becomes a static-guard test that allows only that one file.
- **Verified:** flag constructions and colours from Wikipedia. Neither law fixes the colour values; the hex values are published approximations.

### ADR-0012: Select and date picker, amends ADR-0004
- **Decision:**
  - **Packages:** `@angular/aria@22.3.0` and `@angular/cdk@22.3.0` (both MIT; aria requires exactly cdk 22.3.0).
  - **Select:** `CustomSelect` is a `FormValueControl<string>`. It uses a `<button ngCombobox>` for select-only lists and an `<input ngCombobox>` when the list is searchable (4 or more options).
  - **Date:** `DateField` uses `transformedValue` with a pure `parseDateText`. The calendar is a CDK Dialog; its grid keyboard runs through a pure `nextFocusDate`.
  - **Disabled days:** a day is disabled exactly when `validateField` rejects it, so `minAge` is not re-implemented.
  - **Bundle:** step 1 becomes lazy-loaded (`loadComponent`) to stay under the 500 kB warning.
- **Options:** aria + CDK vs CDK only vs Angular Material 22.3.0.
- **Strongest argument against:** aria has been stable for under six months, had its combobox rewritten in 22.0.0, has had about 24 fixes since, leaves `aria-controls` off a collapsed combobox, and has no date picker.
- **Amendments to ADR-0004:**
  - Driver D7 ("native controls") no longer applies to `select` and `date`.
  - In the implementation note, `syncNative` writes number keys only; date keys are written from the model.
- **Verified:**
  - aria's developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0 (components CHANGELOG, #33232).
  - API checked in the packed package. Combobox works on any element; it is editable only on input and textarea.
  - CDK overlays default to native popovers; jsdom 31.0.1 has no `showPopover` and no `inert`; the CDK Dialog sets `aria-hidden` on the page behind and restores focus.
  - Hazard found: `transformedValue` builds the shown text as `linkedSignal(format(model))`, so storing `''` would erase what the person typed. The ADR prescribes a custom `format` to keep the text.
  - Bundle: aria + CDK +125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer; CDK alone +99.29 kB raw.

### ADR-0013: Motion
- **Decision:** native `animate.enter` with CSS on duration and easing tokens, and no library.
  - **Step change:** enter-only animation on the arriving page, so only one `h1` is ever in the DOM.
  - **Reduced motion:** built in from the start. Every animation or transition is declared inside a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` block, enforced by the guard, and the duration tokens are also 0 under `reduce`.
  - **CDK:** overlays and dialogs use `disableAnimations: true`, because the CDK backdrop keeps a 1 ms transition under reduced motion, which would fail AC-17.
- **Options:** native vs `withViewTransitions()` vs Motion 14.14.0 / GSAP 3.15.1.
- **Strongest argument against:** view transitions give a real cross-fade with one line, while enter-only is a hard cut followed by a fade.
- **Verified:**
  - `animate.enter` is public API since 20.2; `withViewTransitions` is public API only since 22.3.
  - Bundle: Motion +74.10 kB raw / +23.97 kB transfer (`motion/mini` +8.92 / +2.71); GSAP +71.36 / +25.00, and its licence is not OSI-approved.

---

### Example palette (computed with WCAG 2.x relative luminance)

| Role | Hex |
|---|---|
| Page background (ink-950) | `#0B0B14` |
| Surface (ink-900) | `#14131E` |
| Raised surface: header, inputs, panels (ink-850) | `#1D1C2A` |
| Hover (ink-800) | `#272736` |
| Decorative hairline (ink-700) | `#3B3B4C` |
| Control border (ink-500) | `#7E7E93` |
| Muted text (ink-300) | `#BCBCCC` |
| Text (ink-50) | `#F6F6FB` |
| Violet 200 / 300 (focus) / 400 (brand) / 500 (glow) | `#D8D0FF` / `#C0B0FE` / `#AA8FFF` / `#9060FB` |
| Recommended card gradient | `#6427C4` → `#4F1B9E` → `#16154D` |
| Error | `#FF9592` |
| Success | `#74E29F` |
| Primary button | `#FFFFFF` → `#D8D0FF` with `#0B0B14` text |
| Texture | white dots at 7% (worst case composited: `#1C1C24`) |
| Colombia accent | `#FFCD00` |
| Chile accent | `#F66E5E` |

Ratios, worst case first. All pass.

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| Text | 13.63 on hover (15.71 on the texture) |
| Muted text | 7.84 |
| Link | 7.61 |
| Error | 6.97 |
| Success | 9.18 |
| Control border (needs 3:1) | 3.70 on hover, 4.23 on raised |
| Focus ring | 4.14 at the recommended card's top stop, 8.69 on raised |
| Brand / selected | 6.46 |
| Primary button text | 13.42 at the bottom stop |
| White text on the recommended card | 7.99 at the top stop |
| Muted text on the recommended card | 5.47 |
| Check-circle on the recommended card | 4.99 |
| Display heading gradient | 8.77 at the violet stop over the texture |
| Badge text | 10.15 |
| Selected day | 7.54 |
| Colombia accent | 11.17 on the header |
| Chile accent | 5.84 on the header |
| Flag ring | 4.23 |

Raw flag colours do not pass on near-black (Chile blue 1.71, Colombia blue 1.42), which is why the flags get a ring and the Chile accent is a lighter tint of the flag red.

### Example type scale

The sizes are Bringhurst's classic scale: 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 36 and 48.

| Use | Size / line height | Face |
|---|---|---|
| Display (`h1`) | `clamp(2rem, 1.25rem + 3.2vw, 3rem)`, i.e. 32 → 48 px / 1.05 | Archivo 800, width 125, tracking −0.02em, gradient text |
| Price | 36 / 1.1 | Archivo 800, width 112 |
| `h2` | 24 / 1.25 | Archivo 700, width 112 |
| `h3` | 21 / 1.3 | Archivo 700 |
| Lead | 18 / 1.5 | Atkinson 400 |
| Body, inputs | 16 / 1.55 | Atkinson 400; labels and buttons 600 |
| Small | 14 / 1.45 | Atkinson |

Nothing goes below 14 px, there are no all-caps labels, and paragraphs are capped at 68ch.

---

### Spec changes the ADRs force (for the spec-writer after HC1/HC2)
1. **Q-09:** the icon package becomes `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0, not `lucide-angular`.
2. **AC-02:** "card border 3:1" should mean interactive cards only; summary panels keep a decorative hairline, which WCAG allows.
3. **BR-12 and AC-19:** need wording for variable fonts (one file per family, weight range limited) and for the system fallback stack (local fonts, never downloaded).
4. **Q-08 and Q-03:** the spec's starting fonts and colours are replaced by the ADR values. The Chile accent is `#F66E5E`.
5. **§8 vs §8.1:** §8 shows a "Seleccionado" badge on the chosen plan, but §8.1 does not list that string. Add it or drop the badge.
6. **Q-10:** should say "official constructions", not "official designs", because no law fixes the flag colours.
7. **Empty searchable select:** for an `<input>`, the prompt is the placeholder, so `inputValue()` is `''`. This affects AC-05, §11.1 and `expectEmptyStep1`.
8. **AC-09 "page is inert":** the CDK Dialog provides a focus trap, a backdrop and `aria-hidden` on the page behind, not the HTML `inert` attribute. The scenario should assert those.
9. **`aria-controls` while collapsed:** §11.1 expects it on a collapsed select, but aria binds it only while the list is rendered. Relax the assertion, or choose CDK-only for the select.
10. **Monday-first calendar:** CLDR data gives Sunday as the first day for es-CO (Monday for es-CL). The human should confirm Monday for Colombia.
11. **Searchable select on phones:** a bottom sheet opened while the on-screen keyboard is up must fit above it. This needs an HC3 phone check; the fallback (a sheet with its own search box) would need a spec change.
12. **Q-16:** the confirmation check animates with scale and fade, because a stroke "draw" is not transform or opacity, which §9 requires.
13. **BR-01 guard:** must also accept the `(hover: hover)` media feature, used for the card lift.
14. **AC-17:** can assert that `getAnimations()` is empty, not just "no running animation".

### Accepted ADRs amended (only if accepted)
- **ADR-0001**, by ADR-0011: the country-code exception and the new guard that replaces the review grep.
- **ADR-0004**, by ADR-0012: driver D7 for `select` and `date`, and the `syncNative` note for dates.

### Other notes for the developers
- Step 1 becomes lazy-loaded. ADR-0001's addresses are unchanged, and the existing guard only forbids lazy loading in the summary feature.
- Avoid the word "card" in `.ts`/`.html` names, for example `plan-card`. The US-03-AC-15 guard (`/\bcard\b/i`) would trip.
- There is no CSP header in nginx today, so none needs changing.
- Fonts under `/fonts/` get no long-cache header from the current nginx config. That is optional to change and belongs to the frontend developer.

### What I could not verify
- **aria fix count:** "about 24" fixes between 22.0.1 and 22.3.0 is approximate; it comes from a summarised read of the CHANGELOG. The packed typings carry no stability tags, so "stable" rests on the CHANGELOG entry.
- **`aria-controls` after a close:** whether it survives closing the list with `preserveContent` while the list sits inside a CDK overlay template is untested. The developer must check it.
- **Closing animations:** whether `animate.leave` runs when a CDK overlay detaches its content is untested; panels close instantly by default.
- **Windows flag emoji:** that Windows does not draw flag emoji is from general knowledge, marked as such in ADR-0011.
- **View-transition browser support:** I did not verify per-browser support.
- **Material:** Angular Material's bundle size was not measured.
- **Omnibus-Type:** its Buenos Aires origin comes from the foundry's own site.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.

Try to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it – a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each element do exactly one job. A label labels, an example demonstrates, and nothing quietly does double duty.

# Architecture Decision Records

Format: MADR 4 (see the `adr-madr` skill). Only a human sets an ADR to `Accepted` or `Rejected`.
Accepted ADRs are binding (`CLAUDE.md` §1, level 2) and are never rewritten; they are superseded.

## Index

| ADR | Title | Status | Date | Stories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) | Multi-country content strategy and country context (includes wizard routes and step guards) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0006 and ADR-0011) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0003](0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) | Front-end persistence of the wizard state | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0004](0004-forms-library.md) | Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form (Signal Forms over a shared validation core) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0012) | 2026-11-20 | US-01 |
| [0005](0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) | Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01 |
| [0006](0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) | Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01, US-02 |
| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |
| [0008](0008-simulated-payment.md) | Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0009](0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) | Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0010](0010-design-tokens-and-visual-language.md) | Design tokens and visual language: one token file in three tiers, static guard, dark theme, palette with contrast proof, Archivo + Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, `@lucide/angular`, own flag SVGs | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0011](0011-country-visuals-amends-adr-0001.md) | Country visuals (flag and accent) as a presentation-only front-end map (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0012](0012-accessible-select-and-date-picker.md) | Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |
| [0013](0013-motion-and-reduced-motion.md) | Motion with native `animate.enter` and CSS on duration tokens, enter-only step transition, reduced motion by construction | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-04 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0002 | **Terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** ADR-0002 names the US-03 permission `api::terms.terms.find`. Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a content type whose singular and plural names are equal (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`, `validateContentTypesUnicity`: "The plural name … should be unique"), so the type is **`api::term.term`** (singularName `term`, pluralName `terms`, as in CLAUDE.md §6). Consequently: the public permission is **`api::term.term.find`** (no `findOne`), reconciled in bootstrap with the existing three; the router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object (US-01-R2-F03), so `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` covers it; the REST path stays **`/api/terms`**, which must be added to the GET-only allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template` (today `countries|form-fields|plans`). The decision (public `find` only, published-only reads, GET-only proxy, no write token in the browser) is unchanged. | US-03 spec v0.1 (US-03-Q-03, §7.4) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). ## ADR-0012 follow-up: the calendar's first day of the week now comes from the locale

I added an implementation note for ADR-0012 to the index. The accepted ADR file itself is unchanged.

`git status` shows only these two changed files; no commit:
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/README.md`: one new row in "Implementation notes on accepted ADRs".
- `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-04/tasks.md`: the T-04 status now records that ADR-0012 was accepted and the note was added.

### Note text (ADR-0012 row, "Since": Spec v0.2 (ece558e); HC1 2026-11-21)
- **Decision:** ADR-0012 §4 says Monday first, with Home/End going to Monday/Sunday. Instead, the first column is the first day of the week of the current country's locale tag, taken from CLDR through `Intl`: Sunday for `es-CO`, Monday for `es-CL`. Home and End move to the first and last day of that locale's week. The note cites the HC1 decision (2026-11-21) and spec v0.2 (ece558e: BR-06, AC-09).
- **No country code or table:** the date picker receives the locale tag and derives the day from it.
- **How:** `new Intl.Locale(tag).getWeekInfo().firstDay` (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday). If that method is missing, use the older `weekInfo` accessor. If neither exists, use Monday. It is a pure function next to `calendar-dates.ts`.
- **Fallback effect:** on browsers with neither API (Firefox before 153, Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 99), Colombia shows Monday first.
- **Not used:** Angular's `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek`.
- **Unchanged:** the rest of ADR-0012.

### Evidence
- **Browser support (MDN browser-compat-data, `javascript/builtins/Intl/Locale.json`):**

  | Engine | `getWeekInfo()` | `weekInfo` accessor |
  |---|---|---|
  | Chrome | 130 | 99 |
  | Firefox | 153 | none |
  | Safari | 17 | 15.4, removed in Technology Preview |
  | Node.js | 24.0.0 | 18.0.0 |

  It is standard-track and not deprecated.
- **Measured on 2026-11-21** with a scratchpad script using the project's Playwright 1.65.1:

  | Runtime | `getWeekInfo()` | `weekInfo` | es-CO | es-CL | es, es-419 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Chromium 159.0.8154.6 (the only Playwright project in `playwright.config.ts`) | yes | absent (MDN does not record this removal) | 7 | 1 | 1 |
  | Node 24.22.1 (runs Vitest) | yes | yes | 7 | 1 | 1 |

  - Firefox and WebKit are listed in Playwright's `browsers.json` (Firefox 159.0, WebKit 27.2) but are not installed, so I did not run them.
- **World default:** in Node ICU, `und-001` (CLDR's world region) gives Monday (1). Plain `und` gives 7, because it resolves to en-US, so the fallback must be the literal Monday, not `new Intl.Locale('und')`.
- **Why not Angular's `getLocaleFirstDayOfWeek`:** in `@angular/common@22.3.0` (`types/common.d.ts:549-558`) it is `@deprecated 18.0` ("Angular recommends relying on the `Intl` API… `getWeekInfo` … Chromium M99 & Safari 17"). The app also registers no locale data: `registerLocaleData`, `LOCALE_ID` and `@angular/common/locales` do not appear anywhere in `frontend/src`. Using it would mean importing es-CO and es-CL data as a second source.

### Recommendation
Use `getWeekInfo()`, then the `weekInfo` accessor, then Monday. This keeps CLDR as the only source and adds no per-country table. Unit tests run in Node 24 and e2e in Chromium 159, so both get the real CLDR values; tests should still inject the fallback path once.

### What the human must confirm
On browsers with neither API (Firefox before 153, Safari before 15.4, Chrome before 99), Colombia would show Monday first instead of Sunday. Is that acceptable as graceful degradation? The alternative would be a hard-coded table, which the HC1 decision ruled out.

### Not verified
- Behaviour on real Firefox and Safari; I relied on MDN data there.
- Whether recent Safari still ships the `weekInfo` accessor.
